newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua calls recess in presidential vote count.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua calls recess in presidential vote count.

text.p: Nicaragua's highest electoral authority on Wednesday announced a week-long recess in counting votes in disputed presidential elections and said they would announce no official winner until all results have been double-checked.

Rosa Marina Zelaya, head of the Supreme Election Council, told a news conference the final tally would be based on electoral documents collected province-by-province by authorities, and not on summaries of them sent in by radio, fax or telegram.
Preliminary results announced so far, which gave victory to right-winger Arnold Aleman, have been based on the summaries.

"I'm going to give the last report based on telegrams, fax or radio transmission," Zelaya said, announcing that with 87.84 percent of the vote counted from Sunday's election gave Aleman an 11-point lead over his nearest rival, leftist Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega.
The Sandinistas have alleged that "serious irregularities" marred the vote count, pointing out discrepancies between the summaries of results and the documents on which they were based.
Zelaya said she aimed to publish the final tally in full a week from Thursday, but said the process was likely to be slow.
Former revolutionary President Ortega's challenge of the preliminary results had raised fears of social unrest in the country.
